full_judgment:
6. The prosecution examined 17 witnesses including the informant, Doctor who held post-mortem examination on the dead body and the investigating officer who submitted charge-sheet, all of whom were cross-examined by the defence. After close of the cross-examination witnesses the accused on dock were examine under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to which they repeated their innocence and defence did not adduce any evidence. 

 8. The learned trial Court, in consideration of the evidence on record as well as facts and circumstances of the case, however, found the accused-appellants guilty for the offence under section 302 of the Penal Code and, as such, convicted them there under and sentenced them to suffer imprisonment for life and to pay a fine with default cause as mentioned above. The learned trial Court however found the rest accused not guilty for the offence charged and, as such, acquitted them there from. The accused-appellants being aggrieved and dissatisfied thereby have come up with the present appeal which is opposed by the State-respondent through the learned Assistant Attorney-General Mr Rabiul Karim. 

 9. Mr Anisur Rahman Hatem, the learned Advocate for the accused-appellants, took us through the first information report, charge-sheet, charge, post-mortem report, sketch map, deposition of the prosecution witnesses, impugned judgment and other materials papers/documents as available in paper book and submits, that this is a case of no evidence. But the learned trial Court arrived at a decision on guess and surmises. He further submits that the withholding of the independent and disinterested witnesses and having not been examined in this case, nor the prosecution has come up with any reasonable explanation for their absence, led their case unworthy to be believed and for non production of the independent and disinterested witnesses the defence is entitled to get benefit under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act, on the ground that even if they had been examined, they would not have supported the prosecution case. He then submits that prosecution has not been able to prove the place and manner of occurrence. He finally submits that the withholding of independent and disinterested witnesses has cast cloud over the prosecution case and the defence is entitled to get benefit of the defect. 

 27. It appears from the evidence on record that from the place of occurrence to Fulpur Police Station is about 44 kilometres, out of which 14 kilometres is kachcha road and time of occurrence as recorded in first information report is 2-30 PM and the informant who was away from the place of occurrence after hearing the news came to the place of occurrence, saw the dead body of deceased Tota Mia and other injured persons and after hearing about the facts from the witnesses, went to Fulpur Police Station and lodged first information report at 4-45 PM and from inquest report we find that the investigating officer held the inquest of the dead body at 5-50 PM. However, a distance 44 kilometres most of which is kachcha road and without mentioning the name or the means of communication used by the investigating officer as well as the informant who covered a distance of 44 kilometres of kacha road and recording the first information report sitting at the Police Station has created doubt in the prosecution case. 

 28. That from the seizure list it is found that the investigating officer has seized 10 halengas with lati, about 15 to 18 cubes long, 4 bollums with stick 6 cubes long, 2 sulfi joint with stick and another sulfi with lati 7 cubes long, some blood-stained mud from the place of occurrence and 3 iron rods were seized, but from the evidence on record and from the depositions of the prosecution witnesses even from the first information report, it has not been stated that the accused threw away the above mentioned arms, while they fled away from the place of occurrence and it is further noticed that the said weapons were recovered from the alleged place of occurrence. Furthermore, we find that 3 iron rods were recovered by the investigating officer and seized as alamats but in this case from the evidence on record we do not find any such iron rod was used by the accused during the occurrence.
